tools.description: Call this instead of tapping through the simulator by hand: it drives the app through a walkbook on a simulator or physical device, writes a capture bundle, and answers what it reached and refused. A walk takes minutes and nothing is served until it finishes; the answer names every screen the app lacked. 'dryRun' is the cheap check.

animations.description: Keep UIKit animations on (a simulator walk switches them off by default).

appleAudit.description: Record Apple's accessibility audit per state (apple-audit.json); about 2 s a state.

appPath.description: An .app bundle to install first; on a physical device it replaces the phone's copy.

device.description: Simulator name or UDID, or a physical device UDID (needs 'team', no 'dryRun').

dryRun.description: Follow each screen's route against the booted app and report steps that no longer land; captures nothing.

lease.description: Token from `simwalk lease acquire`: walks that device. Instead of 'device'.

motion.description: Record when each capture's tree last changed (ms), with the read cadence and count.

output.description: Bundle directory to write (ends in .simwalk, must not exist); with 'dryRun', a new .json report.

runnerBundleId.description: Physical device only: the runner's bundle id, if the default is not one your team can sign.

screenIDs.description: Walk only these screen ids; the bundle records the subset, so it is not a full walk.

settle.description: Milliseconds the screen must hold still before each capture.

stock.description: Boot a SimWalk-created device (`lease acquire` with `cloneFrom`) with every launchd service on.

team.description: Physical device only, and required there: the Apple signing team ID the runner is built under.

verbose.description: Write the full result file: every state and route.

walkbook.description: Path to a walkbook JSON file.

tools.name: walk

tools.description: Call this before a walk, instead of finding out on the simulator: it answers whether a walkbook parses and can be executed as written, naming every problem at once. Seconds, where a walk costs minutes, but it checks the plan and never the app.

device.description: Apply the physical-device target's rules too: whatever such a walk would refuse is a problem here.

walkbook.description: Path to a walkbook JSON file.

tools.name: validate

tools.description: Call this instead of opening a bundle's screenshots and accessibility trees: it answers what the walk reached, what it refused (and the route), and what is on disk. 'step' reads one screen's text inside the screenshot's frame (not unobscured: text under a bar or sheet counts); shapes need the screenshot. A navigation bar's title names a screen only as a last resort, and says it is localised.

all.description: With 'step': list the off-screen elements too, after the on-screen ones, each marked.

bars.description: With 'step': the tab bars, toolbars and navigation bars with frames; alone, or with 'tree' and 'match'.

bundle.description: Path to a capture bundle directory.

match.description: With 'step': only elements whose label or value contains this (case-insensitive), on or off screen.

state.description: With 'step': which captured state to read, by slug (e.g. 'light'). Default: the first, naming the others.

step.description: Read one screen instead of the manifest: its 1-based position in the walk, or its own id.

tree.description: With 'step' and 'match': the matched nodes with identifier, frame, selected flag and ancestors, not the text.

tools.name: inspect

tools.description: Call this instead of reading a bundle's accessibility trees: it runs every audit rule, one section per rule: disclosure rows not typed as controls, enabled controls with no label or identifier, controls labelled with an SF Symbol name, one label on distinct controls. Seven apple* rules report Apple's own audit, where recorded. Form, never value; it says which screens it could not cover.

bundle.description: Path to a capture bundle directory.

only.description: Run only these rules. Omit for every rule.

walkbook.description: A walkbook whose screens state 'budgets', for the motionBudget and performanceBudget rules.

tools.name: audit

tools.description: Call this instead of opening two walks' screenshots side by side: it compares a run bundle against a reference by form, never value: sections on one side only, reordered, moved or resized; layout shifts on one side only; Apple audit issues only the run has. It says which screens it could not compare. Each flag names a screenshot crop; pass 'crops' to write PNGs and open only those.

crops.description: A new or empty directory for one PNG per flag crop. Omit to get the flags without files.

reference.description: Path to the reference capture bundle.

run.description: Path to the capture bundle compared against the reference.

tools.name: diff

tools.description: Call this instead of reading a bundle's screenshots to check a number: it reads each figure the walkbook names off the captured screens and asks the walkbook's value oracle command what it should be, under every window named. One line per figure per state, saying which window the on-screen figure matches, or none; it names the figures on screens that were not captured.

walkbook.description: Path to the walkbook JSON carrying 'oracle' and each screen's 'figures'.

tools.name: oracle

tools.description: Call this to explore a running app warm instead of paying a runner launch per look: 'start' holds a resident runner on a simulator or physical device you own and prints an id; 'read' answers inspect's screen and a 'screen <hash>'; 'step' takes one route step guarded by that hash (a stale guard is refused); 'save' writes the landed steps as a walkbook screen, before 'end'; 'list' shows sessions.

animations.description: start: keep UIKit animations on (a simulator session switches them off by default).

app.description: start: the bundle id of the installed app.

device.description: start: UDID of a booted simulator that is yours, or a paired physical device (needs 'team'). Or 'lease'.

expect.description: save: the identifier the reached screen carries.

guard.description: step: the screen hash a read printed.

id.description: read, step, save, end: the id start printed.

into.description: save: the walkbook to create or append the screen to (the whole file is re-encoded).

lease.description: start: a lease token from `simwalk lease acquire`.

match.description: read: only the text elements whose label or value contains this.

runnerBundleId.description: start, physical device only: the runner's bundle id, if the default is not one your team can sign.

screen.description: save: the id the saved screen takes.

screenshot.description: read: also write a PNG (point scale, about 450 tokens to view); its path is on a 'screenshot:' line.

screenshotOf.description: read: crop to the element with this label plus 8 pt; implies 'screenshot'.

screenshotScale.description: read: pixels per point, 1, 2 or 3 (default 1); implies 'screenshot'.

since.description: save: only the steps from this request number on.

state.description: start: a walkbook 'states' entry to launch under.

step.description: step: one walkbook route step, e.g. {"tap":{"label":"Next"}}.

team.description: start, physical device only, and required there: the Apple signing team ID the runner is built under.

tools.name: session

tools.description: Call this instead of screenshotting iPhone Mirroring to drive a real iPhone. 'read' answers the screen; 'tap', 'swipe', 'scroll' and 'menu' act and answer; 'burst' taps, then 1-60 frames. Positions are 0-1 fractions of the mirroring window; the answer's line boxes give them. It never types; a drag does not scroll an app, 'scroll' does. Never tap anything that deletes, signs out or disconnects.

at.description: tap, burst: [x, y] fractions of the window. swipe: where it starts. scroll: the pointer (default [0.5, 0.5]).

item.description: menu: Home Screen or App Switcher.

lines.description: scroll: wheel lines, 1-50; positive reveals what is below (or right), negative above.

match.description: read, tap, swipe, scroll, menu: only the text lines that contain this.

ms.description: swipe: how long the drag takes, 50-5000 (default 350).

out.description: A directory to keep the captures in, unpruned.

settleMs.description: read, tap, swipe, scroll, menu: longest wait for the screen to settle, ms (default 3000).

sheet.description: burst: also write sheet.png, the frames tiled and labelled by time.

tools.name: mirror
